input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: After stripping ANSI codes the prompt text is also passed through str.strip(), which removes the whitespace at the end of the prompt that separates it from the user's typed input.
- failure path: click.prompt("Name") builds the prompt 'Name: '; when the stream does not support color (piped output, CliRunner, NO_COLOR) the prompt is shown as 'Name:' with the cursor glued to the colon, while on a color-capable terminal the same call keeps the trailing space, so transcripts differ between the two environments.

Reviewer finding
- description: The prompt text is now `.strip()`ped whenever ANSI stripping applies, which also removes the trailing space that separates the prompt from user input (e.g. "Name: " becomes "Name:").
- rationale: Trigger: a prompt such as "Name: " is shown with stripping enabled, which happens when the stream is not a TTY (piped output or CliRunner). Mechanism: strip() removes the trailing space, so input() renders the prompt without the separator. Impact: prompts on non-TTY streams are formatted differently from the echo-based path and from TTY output, with the cursor directly against the colon. Only the ANSI removal was needed, so the strip() call is an unintended change.
critique: The finding names the same faulty operation: str.strip() is applied after ANSI stripping and removes the trailing space. It describes the same effect, "Name: " becoming "Name:" on non-TTY streams, so output differs from TTY output. That is the labeled mechanism and failure path.
